content: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations published a comprehensive assessment in 2015 on the state of global animal genetic resources for food and agriculture, edited by Scherf BD and Pilling D. Patz JA, Daszak P, Tabor GM, and Aguirre AA, in their 2008 publication in Environmental Health, provided policy recommendations addressing the health risks associated with land-use changes and the emergence of infectious diseases. They emphasized the need for sustainable land management to mitigate these risks. Wall DH, Nielsen UN, and Six J explored the relationship between soil biodiversity and human health in a 2015 article in Nature. Their findings underscore the critical role of soil ecosystems in supporting human well-being and agricultural productivity. Mattei J, Malik V, Wedick NM, Hu FB, Spiegelman D, Willett WC, and colleagues proposed strategies to reduce the global burden of type 2 diabetes by improving the nutritional quality of staple foods. Their 2015 study, published in Globalization and Health, is part of the Global Nutrition and Epidemiologic Transition Initiative. Yang G-J, Utzinger J, and Zhou X-N examined the interplay between environmental factors, agriculture, and infectious diseases in poverty-stricken areas of China. Their 2015 case studies, published in Acta Tropica, highlight the complex interactions between these elements and their impact on public health. Horrigan L, Lawrence RS, and Walker P discussed how sustainable agricultural practices can address the environmental and health harms caused by industrial agriculture. Their 2002 article in Environmental Health Perspectives emphasized the benefits of transitioning to more sustainable farming systems. The High-Level Panel of Experts (HLPE) on Food Security and Nutrition released a report in 2019 advocating for agroecological and innovative approaches to enhance food security and nutrition. This report emphasizes the importance of sustainable food systems in addressing global challenges. Garibaldi LA, Gemmill-Herren B, D’Annolfo R, Graeub BE, Cunningham SA, and Breeze TD, in their 2017 article in Trends in Ecology & Evolution, highlighted farming approaches that promote biodiversity, improve livelihoods, and enhance food security. Birch ANE, Begg GS, and Squire GR, in a 2011 study published in Journal of Experimental Botany, demonstrated how agroecological research can address food security challenges under new integrated pest management (IPM) and pesticide reduction policies. Altieri MA, in a 2004 article in Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment, emphasized the importance of linking ecologists and traditional farmers to develop sustainable agricultural practices. De Filippo C, Cavalieri D, Di Paola M, Ramazzotti M, Poullet JB, Massart S, and colleagues conducted a comparative study in 2010, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, revealing how diet shapes gut microbiota in children from Europe and rural Africa. Gentile CL and Weir TL, in their 2018 Science article, explored the intersection of diet and human health through the lens of gut microbiota, emphasizing its critical role in maintaining overall health. Valdes AM, Walter J, Segal E, and Spector TD, in a 2018 BMJ article, reviewed the role of gut microbiota in nutrition and health, highlighting its influence on metabolic and immune functions. West CE, Renz H, Jenmalm MC, and Kozyrskyj AL, in a 2015 study published in Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, discussed the associations between gut microbiota and inflammatory noncommunicable diseases, as well as the potential for microbiota-based therapies. Zheng-Zheng T, Chen G, Hong Q, Huang S, Smith HM, Shah RD, and colleagues, in a 2019 Frontiers in Genetics article, used multi-omic analysis to uncover microbiome-dependent relationships between diet and metabolites in healthy individuals. Vivarelli S, Salemi R, Candido S, Falzone L, Santagati M, Stefani S, and colleagues, in a 2019 Cancers article, examined the role of gut microbiota in cancer, from pathogenesis to potential therapeutic applications. Hahtela T, in a 2017 article in Porto Biomedical Journal, argued for the medical community to take biodiversity loss seriously due to its implications for human health. Adams C, in a 2018 Journal of Microbiology Biotechnology article, discussed the multifaceted influences of the microbiome on human health, emphasizing its role in disease prevention and management. Singh RK, Chang H-W, Di Yan, Lee KM, Ucmak D, Wong K, and colleagues, in a 2017 Journal of Translational Medicine article, reviewed the influence of diet on the gut microbiome and its implications for human health. Heiman ML and Greenway FL, in a 2016 Molecular Metabolism article, highlighted the importance of dietary diversity in maintaining a healthy gastrointestinal microbiome. Claesson MJ, Jeffery IB, Conde S, Power SE, O’Connor EM, Cusack S, and colleagues, in a 2012 Nature article, demonstrated correlations between gut microbiota composition, diet, and health in elderly populations. Kau AL, Ahern PP, Griffin NW, Goodman AL, and Gordon JI, in a 2011 Nature article, explored the interactions between human nutrition, the gut microbiome, and the immune system. O’Connor EM, in a 2013 Current Opinion in Clinical Nutrition & Metabolic Care article, reviewed the role of gut microbiota in determining nutritional status. Flint HJ, Scott KP, Louis P, and Duncan SH, in a 2012 Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology article, discussed the role of gut microbiota in nutrition and health, emphasizing its impact on metabolic processes. Bäckhed F, Ley RE, Sonnenburg JL, Peterson DA, and Gordon JI, in a 2005 Science article, examined the mutualistic relationship between host and bacteria in the human intestine. Prescott S and Logan A, in a 2018 Challenges article, advocated for integrating biodiversity conservation into the planetary health paradigm to address global health challenges. Logan AC, Jacka FN, and Prescott SL, in a 2016 Current Allergy and Asthma Reports article, identified dysbiosis as a global health issue, emphasizing the need for immune-microbiota interaction research. Rook GAW, Raison CL, and Lowry CA, in a 2014 Clinical and Experimental Immunology article, discussed the role of microbial old friends in immunoregulation and their connection to socioeconomic status. Hanski I, von Hertzen L, Fyhrquist N, Koskinen K, Torppa K, Laatikainen T, and colleagues, in a 2012 Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences article, demonstrated the interrelation between environmental biodiversity, human microbiota, and allergy prevalence. Von Hertzen L and Hahtela T, in a 2006 Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology article, proposed that the disconnection between humans and soil biodiversity may contribute to the asthma and atopy epidemic.
